tier_reason: Upgraded from D: the README cites the peer-reviewed IPDPS 2021 paper (pp. 68-78, doi 10.1109/IPDPS49936.2021.00016), and two search results quoting its abstract say TileSpMV beats Merge-SpMV, CSR5 and BSR on most of the full SuiteSparse collection with up to 2.61x, 3.96x and 426.59x speedups respectively. The paper itself could not be opened (IEEE, doi.org, ResearchGate and the lab's ssslab.cn PDF are egress-blocked), and the repo harness times only TileSpMV with no baseline runs, so this is B per the precedent for peer-reviewed papers confirmed through abstract snippets, not A.

corrections.baseline: Merge-SpMV (Merrill and Garland), CSR5 and BSR SpMV on NVIDIA GPUs, as named in the IPDPS 2021 abstract. The BSR implementation is presumably cuSPARSE bsrmv, but the snippets do not say so, and whether cuSPARSE CSR was also compared is unconfirmed.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Peer-reviewed paper (Niu, Lu, Dong, Jin, Liu, Tan, 'TileSpMV: A Tiled Algorithm for Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication on GPUs', IPDPS 2021, pp. 68-78). According to its abstract as quoted in search results, TileSpMV is faster than Merge-SpMV, CSR5 and BSR on most matrices of the full SuiteSparse Matrix Collection, with up to 2.61x, 3.96x and 426.59x speedups respectively. These are maxima only; average or geomean speedups were not visible. The paper body was not opened, and the repo README has no numbers.
corrections.hardware: Paper, per search-result snippets: NVIDIA A100 (Ampere) and NVIDIA Titan RTX (Turing), all 2757 SuiteSparse matrices; host CPU unknown. README: GPU with compute capability >= 3.5 ('NVIDIA Tesla K40 as tested'), CUDA 11.1, Ubuntu 18.04/20.04.
corrections.workload: SpMV (y = Ax) on NVIDIA GPUs over all 2757 matrices of the SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (per abstract snippets). The matrix is split into 16x16 sparse tiles, and seven warp-level kernels (CSR, COO, ELL, HYB, dense, dense row, dense column) are chosen per tile; nonzeros of very sparse tiles go to a separate matrix, which the repo computes with an embedded CSR5 (src/external/CSR5_cuda). FP64 by default (MAT_VAL_TYPE=double).
corrections.caveats: Paper not opened: IEEE, doi.org, ResearchGate, Semantic Scholar and the lab's PDF at ssslab.cn are blocked from this container. Speedups are 'up to' maxima from the abstract, and the 426.59x maximum against BSR is an outlier typical of matrices that do not suit BSR. Precision per figure, average speedups and the cuSPARSE version are unverified. The repo does not reproduce any comparison: src/main.cu checks one TileSpMV run against a CPU CSR reference, and the CSR5 code is part of TileSpMV, not a baseline. In the current HEAD harness (src/tilespmv_cuda.h), the timed loop has the CSR5 call for the extracted very-sparse nonzeros commented out. Reported runtime and GFlops (computed from all nnzA) therefore leave that work out whenever coototal != 0, and the y checked afterwards would lack those contributions. Whether the paper's numbers came from this harness is unknown. The Makefile builds only sm_86 SASS plus compute_61 PTX, a target that matches neither the README's K40 nor the paper's GPUs. Same-lab follow-up DASP (SC'23) reports beating TileSpMV by 2.09x on average in FP64 on A100 (search-result text only), so this is no longer the lab's fastest SpMV. Last commit 2022-08-12.

notes: I checked the README, src/Makefile, src/main.cu, src/common.h, src/csr2tile.h and src/tilespmv_cuda.h via raw.githubusercontent.com, plus the repo page (Apache-2.0, 13 stars, 4 forks, not a fork, not archived, 48 commits) and the commits page (latest 2022-08-12, so abandoned). License, stars, last commit, usability and compiler flags in the record are correct. An agent with IEEE or ssslab.cn access should confirm average speedups, precision and whether cuSPARSE CSR was a baseline; that could also check for an A-tier artifact.
